newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says no comment on 1-litre car report.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says no comment on 1-litre car report.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp on Wednesday declined to comment on a local report that the carmaker would develop a new one-litre engined car.
Jiji News service reported on Wednesday that Toyota would jointly develop a one-litre car with Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd to sell worldwide after a launch in Japan in 1999.
It said the one-litre car would be built at a second European plant that Toyota plans to bring on-line in 2001.
"We cannot comment about our new product development," a Toyota spokesman said.
Toyota said in March it was considering developing a compact car designed exclusively for the European market that would be smaller than any of the firm's existing models.
Toyota has also said it was considering building a new European plant with start-up by early in the next century.
Toyota has never made one-litre cars. It sells its 1.3-litre Starlet model, the smallest car in the current Toyota line-up, in Japan, Europe, Australia and Latin America.
Demand for smaller cars is growing, especially in Europe, due to their greater fuel-effeciency and lower emissions, industry sources said.

Nissan Motor Co Ltd produces a one-litre car in Japan and Britain. Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd and Suzuki Motor Corp produce one-litre cars in Japan, while a few European manufacturers also produce one-litre cars.
